# Voice notes for Sam

## How I sound
I write short, friendly notes that get to the point. I use contractions and first names. I ask a question when I want a reply.

## Do
- Open with the person's first name and a comma.
- Keep most sentences between 8 and 20 words.
- Use contractions like I'm, we're, and don't.
- Ask one direct question near the end when a reply is needed.
- Sign off with a single word such as Cheers or Thanks.

## Don't
- Don't use exclamation marks.
- Don't open with "I hope this finds you well".
- Don't stack three adjectives in a row.

## Avoid words
leverage
circle back
- synergy

## Examples
[sample-01.txt]
Thanks for sending the draft so fast. I read it twice last night and I think the middle section is the strongest part. The opening still feels slow to me — maybe cut the first two paragraphs and start with the customer story? I'm around all day tomorrow if you want to talk it through.
[sample-02.txt]
We're packing the kitchen this weekend, so dinner at our place is off until the 20th. Honestly, the magic of moving wears off after the third box of mugs. If you still have our ladder, could you drop it by on Saturday morning?
[sample-03.txt]
Three slow miles, three times a week, nothing fancy. What surprised me was how much I missed the quiet. No phone, no podcasts, just the sound of my own breathing and the odd dog barking from a yard. I don't time myself anymore.

## Adjust by channel
Email: Start with the first name. End with Cheers.
Post: Keep it under 60 words. Skip the greeting.
Cover letter: Use full sentences and no slang. Keep the warmth.
